summary: Assess currency pressures, reserves, and intervention choices with practical exchange rate policy training. Explore the five-day course and apply.
lede: Foreign exchange management training helps central bank economists, treasury professionals, and financial analysts assess currency pressures and support policy or market decisions. Participants practise interpreting balance-of-payments data and exchange-rate indicators, reviewing reserve adequacy, comparing intervention options, and presenting evidence-based recommendations through dashboards and policy briefs.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who use exchange rate and external-sector evidence to support policy, treasury, or financial-market decisions. This course is designed for: Central bank economists analyzing exchange rate pressures and policy transmission. Foreign exchange reserve managers assessing liquidity, adequacy, and intervention capacity. Treasury dealers monitoring currency exposures and executing FX market transactions. Monetary policy analysts linking exchange rate movements with inflation forecasts. Balance-of-payments statisticians compiling external accounts using BPM6 concepts. FX market operations officers planning auctions and intervention workflows. Financial stability analysts assessing currency mismatches and foreign exchange liquidity risks. Public debt managers evaluating currency composition and external financing exposure. Bank treasury risk analysts measuring FX positions and market sensitivity. Economic research leads preparing exchange rate policy briefings for decision-makers.
modules: Exchange Rate Regimes and Policy Objectives
Exchange Rate Reporting and Action Planning
prerequisites: Working knowledge of monetary policy, foreign exchange markets, or external-sector analysis is recommended. No coding or programming is required; exercises use spreadsheet-based analysis and provided course scenarios.
